## Global guardrails (apply to every item)

G1. Core primary clone `/Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox` is read-only. Core work uses `make worktree-create BRANCH=... WORKTREE_PATH=...`, then `make agent-write-preflight`. Site work uses a linked worktree of `benchbox-site` on a named branch.
G2. Never `git add -A`. Stage explicit paths. Commit identity is `Joe Harris <joeharris76@gmail.com>`. No agent or co-author trailers.
G3. No Python source files, project/lock files or tooling invocation enters site source or imported history. Documentation prose/code examples about Python, uv and uvx are allowed. No JS/TS source enters core.
G4. No hosted ruleset, required-check name or repo setting changes. Core's `docs` required context keeps its name and keeps reporting. If any step seems to need a settings change, stop and report.
G5. Commit messages, PR titles and PR bodies state the durable reason. No tracker IDs, item IDs, plan or handoff references, or run-local state.
G6. Core protected paths (`scripts/site_inputs.py`, `.github/soundness-paths.txt` entries, `quality/comment-policy.json`, `quality/comment-cleanup-scope.json`, ruleset docs) require the oracle review. Resolve every blocking finding. If the oracle is unavailable, stop.
G7. Merge only after required CI is green and the item's verification rubric passed with observed evidence. Never merge on a failed or skipped required check. Merging a site PR to `main` deploys; verify the rehearsal or the receipt before and the probes after.
G8. Before each production change verify the known-good production receipt and retained site artifact are retrievable. On regression dispatch `gh workflow run deploy.yml -R BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site --ref main -f mode=rollback -f receipt_run_id=<known-good-run>`, verify restoration, receipt and probes, then stop. Never rebuild an old site against a newer bundle as rollback.
G9. Before editing a living policy or spec document that an item quotes, re-read it and diff against the quote. Line numbers cited here are evidence of the research date only.
G10. Producer capability lands first without changing default emission; site consumer support is deployed second; new-schema publication activates only afterward. Every emitted bundle must verify with the currently deployed site. Exact member checks remain fail-closed.
G11. Report only exercised verification. Stored verification commands in items are records to run.

## Stop conditions (any item)

- TypeScript generator output differs from Python output after one fix attempt.
- TPC EULA adjacency check fails.
- Oracle review unavailable or blocking.
- Same-input ownership-cutover diff shows anything except edit URLs; redirect/link changes require a separately reviewed output inventory before being included in the baseline.
- Any deploy gate fails (privacy, explorer compat, snapshot digest, links, origin).
- A ruleset or repository-setting change is needed.
- Any unresolved real secret in filtered history stops; documented placeholder rules must be narrowly equivalent to existing privacy policy.
- The freeze check cannot be proven (a moved path changed after the recorded snapshot SHA).

description:
Prepare canonical GitHub link conversion and legacy browser redirect support without enabling either in production before cutover. Capture complete legacy URLs from a fresh verified baseline bundle/artifact, including TPC_EULA.txt sidecars and /docs/dev copies; do not assume stale cached count 183. Map each to an existing core path pinned to the bundle core_sha; validate paths and fragments against repo-files.json. Do not route site-owned docs assets to core URLs or change blog image behavior. Redirects for non-.html suffixes (.sql/.py/.tpl/.txt) MUST be exercised with actual hosting MIME behavior: writing HTML under those names is not proof of navigation. Retain no query/source-file copying after activation. Prepare mode stays disabled until import so it does not violate earlier unchanged-output gates.
Use directory redirect targets <legacy-name>/index.html emitted in publishStatic (legacy URL can normalize through directory301 to text/html) rather than HTML files named .py/.sql or Astro .py.html. Explicitly exclude redirects in sitemap, Pagefind and objects inventories, preserve /docs/_images behavior, and extend deploy probe manifest to sampled old dotted URLs with status/content-type plus browser destination checks. No separate hosted rehearsal endpoint/settings changes; local actual HTTP/browser smoke before merge and first hosted probe immediately at activation, with existing auto-rollback if hosting differs. Pin legacy redirect targets permanently to archive core SHA rather than floating future bundle SHAs; new authored core references can follow selected bundle SHA.
